editorial:
You follow Sir Lionel Frost, a proud monster hunter who wants respect from snobby adventurers and will do almost anything to get it. He meets Mr. Link, a lonely Bigfoot who speaks politely and wants a friend. Together they travel across oceans and mountains to find Shangri-La, joined by Adelina, a brave widow. The movie feels like a warm, funny road trip with gorgeous stop-motion animation and dry British humor. It is family-friendly but has enough action and heart to keep adults smiling.

The animation is stunning, with tiny details in every frame, and the voice cast brings real charm. The pacing moves quickly, though some jokes land better than others, and the villain feels a bit simple. If you love adventure, clever comedy, and beautiful craft, this is a great pick for families and animation fans.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Lionel, Link, and Adelina reach Shangri-La, but the Yetis reject Link as an outsider. Stenk attacks, and the group fights to escape across the icy valley. Lionel gives up his chance to impress high society and chooses to protect his friends instead. Link survives, picks a new name, and the trio sails away together, proving that belonging matters more than fame.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stop-motion adventure and family comedy.
